final_candidates.decision_summary: Strong escape (z=0.864) combined with excellent structure compatibility (0.892) and ~33% natural mutant frequency in homologs; best balanced escape-plus-viability profile.
High escape (0.901) and the best structure score (0.973), but zero mutant frequency among homologs and low plm temper confidence slightly.
Highest escape score (0.964) and the best plm plausibility among lysine candidates, but no structural coverage and near-zero MSA support keep confidence moderate.

stop_reason.detail: All 4 tool calls have been used across phenotype, structure, plm, and MSA evidence; ranking is stable.

history.rationale: Lysine in the Sa antigenic region (residues ~163-185 of the globular head); charge reversal at surface-exposed Sa sites is a classic antibody-escape mechanism and surface Lys->Glu is usually fold-compatible.
Lys-to-Glu charge reversal in the HA1 antigenic head (Ca2 region, ~163-170) is a classic escape motif; awaiting evidence.
High escape but poor structure compatibility (norm 0.249) and near-zero ESM plausibility suggest a substantial fitness cost; demoted.
Near-zero plm and weak structure (0.249) signal replication risk despite good escape; rejected.

rejection.reason: Near-zero plm and weak structure (0.249) signal replication risk despite good escape; rejected.

history.rationale: Adjacent Sa-site lysine; same escape logic as K169E, providing an alternative if the local context of 169 is unfavorable.
Adjacent to K169 in the exposed loop; charge reversal likely disrupts antibody binding with modest structural cost.
Same liability as K169E: escape-high but structure- and plm-poor; adjacent to K169E so likely shares fitness defect.
Near-zero plm and MSA frequency plus mediocre structure make it inferior to alternatives; rejected.

rejection.reason: Near-zero plm and MSA frequency plus mediocre structure make it inferior to alternatives; rejected.

history.rationale: K157 sits in the Ca/Sa-adjacent antigenic surface (~140s H1 loop); charge reversal there disrupts epitopes while a surface Lys->Glu swap preserves structure.
Surface lysine in Sa/Ca antigenic vicinity; charge swap is a strong escape candidate.
Highest escape prediction (0.964) and the best ESM-1v plausibility among top candidates (0.378); structure evidence unavailable (WT mismatch), so viability relies on plm prior.
Highest escape score (0.964) and best plm (0.378) among lysine candidates, but MSA near-zero and no structure coverage keep it at rank 3.
Creates an N-X-S glycosylation sequon (N173-S174 context) in the Sa region; glycan shielding is a potent HA escape mechanism, though added glycan can carry fitness cost.
Loss of negative charge in head loop is milder escape; reranked down pending evidence.
Good escape (0.881) with neutral ESM plausibility (1.0); structure not applicable, kept as backup.
Perfect plm and good escape, but low MSA frequency and no structure data keep it just outside the top 3.
Introduces a potential N-glycan sequon (N-F-Y) on the globular head near the Ca antigenic region; glycan masking can confer escape with modest structural perturbation.
Potential glycosylation-site-creation (N-X-S/T) near Sa site could shield epitopes, but glycan addition risks fitness cost.
Moderate escape and structure but very low plausibility; retained as a glycan-site hypothesis only.
Escape (0.730) is clearly lower than the lysine cluster and plm/MSA are weak; rejected.

rejection.reason: Escape (0.730) is clearly lower than the lysine cluster and plm/MSA are weak; rejected.

history.rationale: Surface lysine within the Sa antigenic loop; charge reversal likely to disrupt antibody binding while remaining solvent-exposed and structurally tolerated.
Surface lysine in the antigenic head; charge reversal escape candidate.
High escape (0.901) combined with the best structure compatibility (ΔlogP=+0.86, norm 0.973); low ESM score offsets somewhat but structure support suggests retained fitness.
Zero mutant frequency among 169 homologs tempers the strong structure (0.973) and escape (0.901) signals; demoted to rank 2 on viability risk.
Position in the Sb-adjacent head region (~180s); Asn->Lys changes local charge/hydrogen bonding on the epitope surface, a common drift-type substitution.
Asn-to-Lys in Sb region alters local epitope charge; conservative substitution preserving solubility.
Low escape (0.529), worst structure score (0.053), and near-zero plm — fails both halves of the objective.

rejection.reason: Low escape (0.529), worst structure score (0.053), and near-zero plm — fails both halves of the objective.

history.rationale: Lysine in the 180-190 antigenic cluster (Sb region); charge reversal at this exposed epitope is a plausible strong escape substitution.
Sb-site lysine on the 190-helix region; surface-exposed charge reversal.
Strong escape (0.864) with high structural compatibility (norm 0.892, ΔlogP=-0.61), indicating a well-tolerated substitution on the HA surface.
MSA shows E at 185 in 33% of homologs — strong natural tolerance — plus high escape (0.864) and excellent structure (0.892); promoted to rank 1 as the most balanced candidate.
Second lysine in the Sb cluster; same escape rationale as K185E, giving an alternative surface-charge flip in a known epitope.
Adjacent Sb-site residue; similar rationale as K185E.
Moderate escape (0.877) and middling structure (0.588) with very low plm; below the top three.
Moderate MSA support (0.114) and decent structure/escape, but very low plm keeps it as backup.
Asn in the Ca-region (~220s loop near the receptor-binding subdomain edge); charge addition on this surface could alter Ca epitopes while keeping the residue surface-exposed.
Charge introduction near receptor-binding region; escape possible but RBS proximity raises fitness risk.
Structure-compatible but escape prediction (0.519) is too low to merit retention.
